title: Electronics, STM32 Firmware and the SBUS Remote-Control Link

blocks.text: This chapter covers the part of the digital twin that Phase 1 exercises most directly: the path from the operator's transmitter sticks to the speed commands that the two traction ESCs receive over CAN. It describes the electronics architecture, the RC link simulation (`RC_Link_Sim`), the STM32H743 firmware model (`Shaddad_MCU`) with its SIM and HW IO variants, and the RC latency budget. Names, parameters and design numbers in this chapter come from the build scripts in `scripts/build/`, the MATLAB function files in `subsystems/` and `scripts/scenarios/`, the parameter files `params/param_electronics.m` and `params/param_rc.m`, the interface control document `docs/icd.md` and the design decisions in `docs/architecture.md` (D-numbers). Results come from `docs/STATUS.md` and the saved runs in `work/results/`.

In Phase 1 (`VC_PHASE = 1`) the chain is: operator, transmitter, 2.4 GHz radio, receiver, SBUS bytes on a UART, MCU SBUS decoder, RC mapping, mode manager and safety supervisor, vehicle control, CAN1 DRV_CMD frames, ESCs. `GNC_Stub` replaces the companion computer. It sends no COMP_CMD frames, so the MCU never sees a healthy companion and AUTO cannot be armed.
Electronics Architecture

The model contains three programmable control units and two kinds of commercial drive controller. Each programmable unit is a separate Simulink model, so it can later be code-generated for its own board. The MCU is the single mode authority. RC commands, companion commands and every supervisor fault pass through it, and the hardware E-stop chain works independently of all software. {tab:tab_ecus} lists the units. The MCU is developed on the STM32H743ZIT6 of a NUCLEO-H743ZI2 board; production uses the STM32H743VIT6 on a custom carrier.

blocks.text: Networks and Links

CAN1 (FDCAN1) is classic CAN 2.0B at 500 kbit/s with 11-bit IDs and little-endian payloads. It connects the MCU, both ESCs, the implement ECU and the BMS, at about 21 % bus load. CAN2 (FDCAN2) is a point-to-point CAN-FD link to the companion, at 1 Mbit/s arbitration and 2 Mbit/s data rate with bit-rate switching. The SBUS receiver is wired to USART2. {tab:tab_links} lists the frames.

blocks.text: Every ECU packs and unpacks its CAN frames in its common logic with `Byte Pack` / `Byte Unpack` blocks. The same codec runs in SIM and HW (D6), so every simulation exercises the real frame encoding. On the plant side, `CAN1_Net_Sim` and `Link_MCU_GNC` route the frames and can drop or delay them for fault injection. Only the `FDCAN Read` / `FDCAN Write` driver blocks are specific to the HW variant.

All DO bits at 0 is the safe state, which is also the state during an MCU reset.
Safety Architecture

items: **Hardware E-stop chain (independent of software).** The front and rear dual-channel mushroom E-stops feed the safety relay in `Power_Plant/Safety_Chain`. When the loop opens, Safety_OK drops: both ESCs enter STO (torque off at once, spring brakes engage) and K3 opens. The contactor coil supply (Safety_HV_OK) drops 1.5 s later.
**MCU contribution.** DO0 MCU_SAFETY_OK is a watchdog-relay contact in the E-stop loop. It can open the loop but can never close it. DO1 SAFETY_RESET_REQ is the 50 ms re-arm pulse for the relay.
**Remote E-stop (CH12).** This is a software stop, because SBUS is not safety-rated. The MCU decelerates at 2.0 m/s² and latches ESTOP. It does not replace the hardware chain.
**Controlled stop.** RC link loss, receiver failsafe, the arm switch going off and class-B faults bring the robot to standstill at 1.0 m/s². The MCU then returns to STANDBY.
**Watchdog.** IWDG1 resets the MCU after 50 ms without a refresh, and all DO lines go low. The ESCs apply their own 100 ms CAN-command timeout as well.

blocks.text: RC Link Simulation

`Shaddad_System/Operator_RC` is a Subsystem Reference to `subsystems/rc/RC_Link_Sim.slx`, which `scripts/build/build_rc_link.m` generates. Its inputs are `op` (`Bus_OperatorCmd`, 10 ms) and `flt` (`Bus_FaultInject`, 10 ms). Its main output, `sbus` (`Bus_SbusStream`, 1 ms), holds up to 32 bytes, a length and a UART-error flag. This is exactly what the STM32 `UART/USART Read` block returns on hardware. A second output, `rc_frame` (`Bus_RcFrame`), is a logging copy of the receiver frame. Inside the file ({fig:F05_rc_link_sim_split.png}), the inputs pass a deterministic rate-transition chain 0.01 s, 0.001 s, 0.014 s. The 14 ms frame rate never leaves the file (D32). {tab:tab_rc_units} lists the units.

blocks.text: Operator Inputs and the Operator Console
`Bus_OperatorCmd` carries the operator's intent: normalised stick values and switch positions, 15 elements at 10 ms. The transmitter maps each element to its SBUS channel ({tab:tab_opcmd}).

blocks.caption: Bus_OperatorCmd elements and their SBUS channels
Shaddad_System/Operator_Console. The Variant Source OpSource selects the scenario input op_ext (VC_OPSRC = 1), the Dashboard subsystem (2) or the joystick placeholder constant P.scen.dash (3).

blocks.text: The Variant Source `OpSource` in `Operator_Console` selects where `Bus_OperatorCmd` comes from ({fig:F13_operator_console.png}). The choice is made with `VC_OPSRC`:

items: `VC_OPSRC = 1` (default): `ScenarioIn.op`, the time table that the scenario files write with `scn_rc_tab` and `scn_rc_stick`. `phase1_test_drive` and every acceptance scenario drive the robot this way. `scn_rc_stick` inverts the RC mapping chain, so a maneuver plan [t v ω] reaches the MCU as v and ω to within one raw count of transmitter quantisation (the second output of `scn_rc_stick` gives the decoded value).

`VC_OPSRC = 2`: the `Dashboard` subsystem. It has 15 Constants (`P.scen.dash.<element>`) bound to Simulink dashboard blocks: throttle and steering Sliders, a speed Knob, a MANUAL / HOLD / AUTO Rotary Switch, Toggle Switches for arm, remote E-stop and transmitter power, and a reset Push Button.

`VC_OPSRC = 3`: a joystick placeholder. `vrlib/Joystick Input` failed its smoke test in R2026b (Simulink 3D Animation is not installed), so this choice is a Constant `P.scen.dash`: transmitter on, sticks neutral, disarmed.

blocks.text: With the dashboard, the robot responds at the Normal-mode real-time factor of about 0.3-0.5, so it moves slower than the wall clock. No interactive dashboard session was part of the Phase 1 acceptance runs [TBD - interactive dashboard drive not verified, docs/STATUS.md].
SBUS Frame and Line Format

An SBUS frame is 25 bytes: a header, 22 payload bytes that carry 16 channels of 11 bits each, a flags byte and a footer ({tab:tab_sbus_frame}). SBUS has no checksum. {tab:tab_sbus_line} gives the line parameters. {fig:F34_sbus_frame.png} shows one decoded frame.

Radio, Receiver and UART Line Timing

When the radio channel marks a frame as lost, the receiver keeps sending the last good channels with frame_lost = 1. After 1.0 s of continuous loss it switches to its failsafe mode. In the default FLAG_PRESET mode it sends frames with failsafe = 1 and the preset channels: sticks 992, mode 992 (HOLD), arm 172 (off) and E-stop 172 (RUN). The E-stop preset is RUN so that a failsafe frame can never latch ESTOP (D34).

`sbus_uart_line_sim.m` turns each released frame into a queue of bytes. Byte i completes at t0 + i·120 µs. The start time t0 includes a sub-millisecond phase (0.37 ms initially) that advances by 2.8 µs per frame (200 ppm of the 14 ms period, modulo 1 ms). Each 1 ms tick outputs the bytes completed since the previous tick, so a 3.0 ms frame arrives in three or four chunks of up to 8-9 bytes (5, 8, 8 and 4 bytes with the initial phase), as the hardware UART Read returns them. A byte error flips one bit of the byte. A single flipped bit always violates even parity, so the chunk that contains it is flagged with `uart_err`. A byte drop removes the byte from the queue. {tab:tab_rc_faults} lists the RC link fault inputs.

blocks.text: MCU Firmware Model (Shaddad_MCU)

`models/Shaddad_MCU.slx` is the STM32H743 firmware. It sits as a Model block in `Shaddad_System`. `scripts/build/build_shaddad_mcu.m` generates it from Subsystem Reference units in `subsystems/electronics/`: `build_fw_platform.m` builds the platform units and `build_fw_control.m` builds the control units. The model ({fig:F03_mcu_top_overview.png}, numbers as in {tab:tab_tasks}) is fixed-step discrete and multitasking, with a 1 ms base rate. It has one root input bus per rate (`in1k`, `in5`, `in10`, `in50`, `in100`), which enters the `IO_In` variant, and five matching outputs from `IO_Out`. A sixth output, `telem` (`Bus_FwTelemetry`, 10 ms), carries firmware internals for logging. The control logic runs in single precision, and integer types are used at the hardware boundary.

blocks.text: {tab:tab_tasks} lists the tasks. Every signal that crosses a task boundary passes an explicit Rate Transition with data integrity and determinism on. For example, `RT_rc_dec` carries the decoded RC data from Task_1k to Task_10, and `RT_mode_1k`, `RT_fault_word_1k` and `RT_alive10` carry the mode, the fault word and the alive counter back to Task_1k ({fig:F03_mcu_top_detail.png}). {fig:F04_mcu_task10_overview.png} and {fig:F04_mcu_task10_detail.png} show the content of Task_10. Task_10, Task_50 and Task_100 each increment an alive counter, and the watchdog manager in Task_1k checks how long ago each of these three counters last changed. The WCET values are design estimates at 480 MHz (`P.electronics.target.mcu.task_wcet`). Together they give a CPU load of about 20 %, against a 50 % acceptance limit. Execution Profiler or PIL measurements will replace them once code generation is available.

blocks.text: SBUS Decoder
`fw_sbus_decoder` runs in Task_1k ({fig:F06_sbus_decoder.png}). Each 1 ms it receives the chunk of bytes that the UART delivered and processes it in three stages:

items: **Frame sync.** The MATLAB Function `Frame_Sync` calls `subsystems/electronics/sbus_frame_sync.m`. It hunts for the 0x0F header, collects 25 bytes and resynchronises after 2 empty ticks (`P.electronics.sbus.gap_ticks`). It outputs the 22-byte payload, the flags byte, a `frame_new` pulse and the counters `n_ok`, `n_bad` and `n_skip`.

**Unpack.** The Enabled Subsystem `Latch` runs on `frame_new`. A commutil2 Integer to Bit block (8 bit, LSB first) and a Bit to Integer block (11 bit, LSB first, uint16) produce `ch_raw[16]`, and the flags byte is split into CH17, CH18, frame_lost and failsafe. `Latch` also updates the link-quality filter, lq = lq + 0.05·(good - lq), once per frame.

**Link supervision.** `rc_age` counts 1 ms ticks since the last valid frame, that is, a frame with frame_lost = 0 and failsafe = 0. It saturates at 10 s and starts saturated. The decoder sets `rc_link_lost` when rc_age exceeds 0.10 s, `rc_ok` when the link is not lost and there is no failsafe, and `lq_warn` when lq drops below 0.70.

blocks.caption: fw_sbus_decoder (Task_1k). MATLAB Function Frame_Sync, the Latch enabled subsystem (unpack, flags, link quality), the rc_age counter, the link-loss and rc_ok logic, and the output bus rc_dec.

blocks.text: A frame is accepted only if all of the following hold:

items: The 0x0F header is at index 0, exactly 25 bytes arrive before the inter-frame gap, and no further byte follows the footer in the same 1 ms chunk.
No chunk that delivered a byte of the frame has a UART error.
The footer is 0x00, or an SBUS2 footer with (footer AND 0x0F) = 0x04, and the reserved flag bits 4-7 are zero.
Every 11-bit channel is within 172..1811 (`P.electronics.rcmap.raw_min` / `raw_max`).

blocks.text: All checks finish on the tick that delivers the last byte, so validation adds no latency.

**Corrupted-frame fix (revision C, 2026-10-23).** Before the fix, the parser reset on a UART error before it consumed the flagged chunk. A bit error in the chunk that starts a frame (bytes 1-9: header and CH1-CH5) was therefore accepted, and S6c showed a stick glitch of 1.25 times full scale: bit 10 of CH1/CH2 had flipped. The error now taints every frame that has a byte in the flagged chunk, including a frame that starts in it. The length and channel-range checks were added at the same time. With 1 % byte errors, S6c now accepts 788 frames, rejects 302 and shows no channel glitch.

blocks.text: {tab:tab_rc_map} gives the channel assignment. The channel map is a parameter, not wiring. It is set by `P.rc.ch_map` on the transmitter side and `P.electronics.rcmap.ch` on the MCU side, and the two must be identical. The transmitter reorders its signals with a Selector driven by `P.rc.tx_perm`.
RC Mapping
`fw_rc_mapping` (Task_10) turns the raw channels into commands. It is built from library blocks only:

x      = sat((raw - 992)/819.5, -1, 1)          % Bias + Gain + Saturation
x_db   = deadzone(x, +/-0.05)/(1 - 0.05)        % Dead Zone + Gain
y      = e*x_db^3 + (1 - e)*x_db                % Polynomial [e 0 1-e 0], e = 0.20 thr / 0.35 steer
s      = 0.25 + (x_CH7 + 1)/2*(1 - 0.25)        % speed scale 25..100 %
v_rc   = y_thr*v_max_man*s                      % v_max_man = 2.0 m/s
w_rc   = -y_steer*w_max_man*s                   % w_max_man = 1.0 rad/s, stick right -> clockwise
pos    = 1 + (x > -0.5) + (x > 0.5)             % 3-position switches
sticks_neutral = abs(x_thr) < 0.08 && abs(x_steer) < 0.08
override       = (abs(x_thr) > 0.30 || abs(x_steer) > 0.30) for > 0.2 s

A 3-position switch position is accepted only when the last 4 samples agree (Tapped Delay debounce, 40 ms, about three SBUS frames). A 2-position switch is ON when x > 0. The remote E-stop on CH12 has no channel debounce. An Enabled sample-and-hold updates it only on frames with frame_lost = 0 and failsafe = 0, so a failsafe frame can neither trigger nor clear it. Example: at full speed scale, a throttle stick of 0.5 gives x_db = 0.474, y = 0.400 and v_rc of about 0.80 m/s. The output `rc` is a virtual bus. It also carries the link status (rc_ok, rc_age, lq, frame counters) to the downstream units.
Mode Manager

`fw_mode_manager` (Task_10, {fig:F15_mode_manager_overview.png} and {fig:F15_mode_manager_detail.png}) wraps the MATLAB Function `Mode_FSM`, which calls `subsystems/electronics/mcu_mode_manager.m`. Stateflow is not installed, so the state machine is written as an ordered transition table. It keeps its state in persistent variables as `ShaddadMode` codes (uint8: 0 BOOT, 1 SELFTEST, 2 STANDBY, 3 MANUAL, 4 HOLD, 5 AUTO_START, 6 AUTO, 7 CTRL_STOP, 8 ESTOP, 9 FAULT), and all its timers count 10 ms ticks. {fig:F20_mcu_modes.png} shows the states and {tab:tab_modes} the transitions. Its inputs are the RC bus, the fault word and fault classes of the same sample, the companion status, BMS HV_Ready and DI bits. The blocks around it compute `standstill` (|v_track| < 0.05 m/s) and `selftest_ok` (ESC and BMS frames fresh, IMU valid, 24 / 12 / 5 V rails above their minimum values).

blocks.text: The mode manager has five outputs:

items: `cmd_src`: RC in MANUAL, AUTO in AUTO, NONE otherwise. HOLD therefore holds zero speed with the drives enabled.
`drive_enable`: true in MANUAL, HOLD, AUTO_START, AUTO, CTRL_STOP and ESTOP.DECEL.
`mode`: the current ShaddadMode code.
`rearm_req`: a one-sample pulse on SELFTEST entry and on every reset edge.
`bms_req` [HV_Enable_Req, Charge_Enable_Req, Fault_Reset_Req, Shutdown_Req] for the BMS_REQ frame. HV_Enable_Req = key on AND no class-A fault AND mode not BOOT or FAULT.

blocks.text: **Arming rules.** The robot moves only under these rules:

items: A move needs a rising edge of the arm switch (CH6) while the link is good. Holding the switch on is not enough.
MANUAL also needs both sticks within ±0.08 of neutral at the arm edge, so the robot cannot jump when it is armed.
After every stop (CTRL_STOP, ESTOP, FAULT) the operator must switch the arm switch off and on again. A returning RC link never restarts motion by itself.
While the link is not good, the mode manager holds the last valid CH5 and CH6 values. Failsafe presets never act as operator commands.

To leave ESTOP: return CH12 to RUN (or release the mushroom button), press reset at standstill (CH9 or the DI reset button), wait for STANDBY, then switch the arm switch off and on with the sticks neutral.
In Phase 1, CH5 = AUTO can never arm. GNC_Stub sends no COMP_CMD, so comp_ok stays false, and a change from MANUAL to AUTO goes to HOLD.

blocks.text: Safety Supervisor and Watchdog

`fw_safety_supervisor` (Task_10) evaluates 32 conditions every 10 ms and packs them into `fault_word` (uint32, ICD section 6). Each bit has a persistence time, implemented as an integer tick counter (Sum + Unit Delay + Switch). Latched bits also have a set/reset latch that clears only on reset_req while the condition is gone. The unit has three more outputs: `warn_word` (the instantaneous conditions), the class flags [A B C], and the derate `k_der`. `k_der` is the minimum of the active derates and of an enclosure-temperature table. {tab:tab_fault_classes} gives the fault classes and {tab:tab_fault_bits} the individual bits.

IMU invalid or |acc| outside 5-15 m/s² (0.5 s)
Implement ECU fault or timeout (0.2 s)

blocks.text: Bits 5, 6, 9 and 28 are monitored from STANDBY on, because no frames exist yet in BOOT and SELFTEST. IMU_FAULT also switches off the yaw-rate loop.

`fw_watchdog_mgr` (Task_1k) refreshes the watchdog only while the alive counters of Task_10, Task_50 and Task_100 have changed within the last 20, 60 and 200 ms (`P.electronics.wdg.age_lim`). On hardware, the refresh writes 0xAAAA to IWDG1->KR (50 ms timeout). In simulation, `Electronics_Plant/Watchdog_Reset_Sim` (`elp_watchdog_reset.slx`) resets the MCU after 50 ms without a refresh and holds it in reset for 0.3 s, with all DO and PWM outputs forced to 0. It then pulses `reset_flag`, which returns the mode manager to BOOT.

The same unit computes DO0 MCU_SAFETY_OK = task ages healthy AND (fault_word AND maskDO0) = 0 AND mode ≠ BOOT. `maskDO0` covers only MCU-internal health: bits 5-8, 23 and 25. Bits 0, 27, 29 and 31 are consequences of the hardware chain. They stop the robot but are excluded from DO0, because otherwise the relay could never re-close (D30). DO1 SAFETY_RESET_REQ is a 50 ms pulse issued after DO0 has been high for 20 ms, once on SELFTEST entry and again on every reset edge. The S0 re-run of 2026-10-23 at 20:47 (`S0_20261023_204711.mat`) measured this sequence: DO0 high at 0.02 s, the 50 ms re-arm pulse, Safety_OK at 0.061 s, HV_Ready at 0.5 s and STANDBY at 1.01 s (PASS, 11 of 11 criteria).
Vehicle Control
`fw_vehicle_ctrl` (Task_10) converts the arbitrated command into the two ESC setpoints. Its steps, in order:

items: **Arbitration.** A Multiport Switch on `cmd_src` selects the RC command (v_rc, ω_rc), the AUTO command, or zero (NONE). The AUTO command is the COMP_CMD v and ω, limited to -0.5..1.5 m/s and ±1.2 rad/s, and it is used only while cmd_valid is true and no soft stop is requested.

**Limits.** v_target is limited to ±k_der·2.0 m/s. ω_target is limited to ±min(k_der·ω_max, a_lat_max / max(|v_ref|, 0.1 m/s)) with a_lat_max = 1.0 m/s² and ω_max = max(w_max_man, w_max_auto) = 1.2 rad/s (the RC mapping already limits manual commands to 1.0 rad/s).

**Reference shaper per axis** (`Shaper_v`, `Shaper_w`). The tracking law is `a_dem = sat(K*(x_t - x_ref), -a_dn, a_up)`, with direction-aware limits. A jerk limit (Rate Limiter Dynamic) and a Forward-Euler integrator follow. The integrator is reset to the measured value while the drive is disabled. CTRL_STOP and ESTOP.DECEL use the constant-deceleration law `a_dem = -sign(x_ref)*min(a_stop, sqrt(2*j*abs(x_ref)), abs(x_ref)/Ts)` (D33). The MCU shaper is the only deceleration limiter in the chain: the ESC ramp of 2.24 m/s² is above every profile. {tab:tab_shaper} gives the profiles by mode.

**Yaw-rate PI** on the bias-corrected gyro z axis. A Discrete PID Controller in PI form (Kp 0.4, Ki 2.0, output ±0.4 rad/s, clamping anti-windup) gives `w_mix = w_ref + u`. The loop makes the closed-loop yaw response first order (τ about 0.25 s) despite skid-steer slip. It is switched off on IMU_FAULT. The gyro bias is re-estimated (τ 2 s) only while both tracks are below 0.02 m/s, so a pivot turn never enters the bias.

**Skid-steer mixer.** `v_L,R = v_ref -/+ w_mix*chi*B/2` and `a_L,R = a_ref -/+ alpha_ref*chi*B/2`, with track gauge B = 0.85 m and the identified effective-gauge factor χ = 1.336 (`P.structure.track.chi_nom`), so χB/2 = 0.568 m. Both are divided by k = max(1, max|v_L,R| / 2.0 m/s). This keeps the path curvature when one track would saturate.
**ESC setpoints.** The motor speed setpoint is `w_ref = (N/r_s)*v_track_ref`, 187.5 rad/s per m/s (N = 24, r_s = 0.128 m). The torque feedforward is `tau_ff = Kff_a*a_track_ref`.

**Torque and power limits.** `tau_lim_mot = min(T_peak, tau_avail, (P_dis/2)*eta_drv/w_star)*k_tr*k_der` and `tau_lim_reg = min(T_peak, (P_chg/2)/(eta_drv*w_star))`, with P_dis = 0.95·V_pack·DCL - 120 W, P_chg = 0.95·V_pack·CCL + 120 W and w_star = max(|ω_m|, 20 rad/s). The BMS charge-current limit therefore limits regeneration without limiting traction. Both limits are zero while the drive is disabled.

**Traction control.** A slip relay (on at 0.30, off at 0.20) and a rate limiter act on k_tr (minimum 0.5). It needs the companion's ground-speed estimate (v_ground_valid), so it is inactive in Phase 1.

blocks.text: CAN Output to the ESCs

Every 10 ms the MCU sends DRV_CMD_L (0x201) and DRV_CMD_R (0x202) through `CAN1_Codec` ({tab:tab_drv_cmd}). The frames carry mode 1 SPEED, enable = drive_enable, park_req = NOT drive_enable and fault_reset = reset request. Each ESC closes its own 1 kHz speed loop on w_ref.

blocks.caption: DRV_CMD payload (docs/icd.md section 4)
rows: b0 enable, b1 park_req, b2 fault_reset, b3-4 mode (0 OFF, 1 SPEED, 2 TORQUE), b8-15 alive counter

blocks.text: The ESC answers with three feedback frames. DRV_FB1 (10 ms) carries status, speed, torque estimate and DC current. DRV_FB2 (50 ms) carries DC voltage, iq, temperatures and `tau_avail`. DRV_FB3 (10 ms) carries the encoder count, fault code and state. Two timeouts apply. The ESC enters QUICK_STOP after 100 ms without a new alive value, and the MCU raises DRV_x_TIMEOUT (class A) after 50 ms without FB1 or FB3. The ESC's `tau_avail` caps `tau_lim_mot`. Since the fix of 2026-10-23, the ESC computes `tau_avail = min(TauThMot, TauDcm)` from its own thermal and DC-current limits (`build_drive.m`, Torque_Limiter), so the MCU's commanded limit is no longer fed back into it. Before this fix, the feedback held the torque at zero, and the robot did not move in S1.
Telemetry

`fw_telemetry` assembles `Bus_FwTelemetry` (38 elements, mostly single precision with integer and boolean status fields, 10 ms) on the MCU's sixth output, and `Shaddad_System` logs it as `telem`. The decoder output is also logged inside the MCU as `rc_dec`, and RC_Link_Sim logs the receiver frame as `rc_frame`. In Phase 2 the MCU also reports to the companion over CAN2. MCU_STATUS (0x200, 50 ms) carries the mode, cmd_src, RC mode switch and aux command, link flags, drive_ready, fault and warning words, track speeds, the applied v and ω, RC link quality and enclosure temperature. MCU_IMU (5 ms), MCU_ODOM (10 ms) and MCU_POWER (100 ms) are sent as well. In Phase 1, GNC_Stub terminates these frames. {tab:tab_telem} lists the telemetry signals most useful for Phase 1 analysis.

SIM and HW IO Variants

Only `IO_In` and `IO_Out` differ between simulation and hardware. Both are Variant Subsystems controlled by `VC_TARGET` (0 SIM, 1 HW, activated at update diagram), and their choices are Subsystem References. The SIM choices `fw_io_in_sim` / `fw_io_out_sim` contain only pass-throughs, Data Type Conversions and Bus Creators. The HW choices `fw_io_in_hw` / `fw_io_out_hw` use STM32 blocks from `stm32h7xxblockslib`, `stmutilitieslib` and `stm32IMUsensorslib`. Every task, codec and safety function is common to both, so a simulation runs the same firmware logic that would be deployed. {tab:tab_io_variants} compares the two variants signal by signal.

**Board builds are blocked.** Simulink Coder is not installed on the build PC (a licence seat exists), and STM32CubeMX, STM32CubeCLT and the GNU Arm tools are missing. The MCU model update with `VC_TARGET = 1` is blocked only by the missing STM32CubeCLT. Board builds of every ECU remain blocked by Simulink Coder (D31). Every simulation in this report uses `VC_TARGET = 0`.
RC Latency Budget

Decision D37 defines two latency measurements. The first runs from the TX frame emission (the transmitter sample) to the DRV_CMD frame at the MCU output. The second runs from the operator stick in `ScenarioIn` to the ESC speed reference. {fig:F19_rc_signal_chain.png} shows the chain and {tab:tab_latency} the budget.

blocks.text: The 14 ms stage is a modelling choice. The deterministic Rate Transition from the frame period to 1 ms after the encoder releases each frame one period late, and this delay stands for the radio latency of a real link. `P.rc.extra_delay_frames = 0` adds no further delay. The budget leaves 2 ms of margin on the 30 ms criterion, and the 14 ms frame period dominates it. The 7 ms high-speed SBUS option was not evaluated in Phase 1.

`phase1_test_drive` forces the sticks to neutral after an E-stop or RC loss and switches the arm switch off and on after the reset or link return, so these runs demonstrate the full restart sequence.
Changing Parameters

Every block reads its values from `P`. `shaddad_params` assembles `P` from `params/param_electronics.m` (`P.electronics`) and `params/param_rc.m` (`P.rc`). To change a value, edit the parameter file and rerun `shaddad_startup` (or `shaddad_params`), so that the base-workspace `P` is refreshed before the next run. A parameter change needs no model rebuild. {tab:tab_el_params} lists the parameters changed most often.

blocks.text: Rebuilding Units

The models are generated by scripts. Do not edit them by hand: the next build overwrites the change. Close `Shaddad_System` before you rebuild. `build_rc_link` refuses to rebuild a file that a loaded model references.

build_rc_link('ssr');                       % RC_Link_Sim and its five units
build_fw_platform({'fw_sbus_decoder', 'fw_rc_mapping'});   % selected units
build_fw_control();                         % supervisor, modes, vehicle control, aux, watchdog
build_shaddad_mcu('model');                 % MCU top model only (units must exist)

The MATLAB Function blocks call `sbus_frame_sync.m`, `mcu_mode_manager.m` and `sbus_uart_line_sim.m` in one line each. An edit to one of these files therefore takes effect at the next model update, without a rebuild.
Before you rebuild any MCU unit, read the warning in {sec:ch08_user_manual/Regenerating models}: `build_shaddad_mcu()` without an argument replaces the five MCU control units with stubs.
